author: mvafin
title: Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode
failed_jobs.symptom: Ninja build of ov_template_func_tests and several sample executables fails with repeated MSVC cl.exe 'fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space' and linker 'LNK1102: out of memory' during the Cmake build - CC COLLECT step.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status check fails because Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode failed upstream.

C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\vector(2202): fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space

root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation (CC) Release build runs with high ninja parallelism on a memory-constrained self-hosted/hosted Windows runner. Once several parallel cl.exe/link.exe processes are active simultaneously compiling template functional tests and sample executables, available heap/virtual memory is exhausted, causing MSVC's cl.exe to emit 'fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space' and link.exe to emit 'fatal error LNK1102: out of memory'. This is the 15th recorded occurrence of the identical signature (first seen 2026-11-03), confirming it is an infrastructure/runner capacity issue rather than a code defect introduced by PR #39608 (a small, unrelated PyTorch FE accuracy fix to log1p/expm1 touching only 3 files).
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reliably reproducible outside the CI runner's exact memory/parallelism conditions; locally reproducible only by building the same CMake CC configuration with an equally high ninja -j parallelism on a machine with comparable (constrained) RAM, e.g. `cmake --build build-modules/template --target ov_template_func_tests -- -j<high>` on a <=16GB Windows VM.
recommended_actions: Reduce ninja/MSBuild parallelism (-j) for the Windows CC build job to a level proportional to available runner RAM (rule of thumb: 1.5-2 GB per parallel MSVC process for Release builds with heavy templates).

Investigate switching large template-heavy functional test compilation units to use /Zm (increase precompiled header memory allocation) or split heavily templated test files (e.g., op_reference/*.cpp) into smaller translation units.
Consider moving this job to a larger-memory runner SKU, given 15 occurrences since 2026-11-03.
Disable or reduce ccache/parallel linking concurrency specifically for the CC Release configuration, since linker LNK1102 failures also occur concurrently with compiler OOM.

Track this as a known recurring infrastructure issue in a tracking ticket referencing this pattern (signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e) so it is prioritized for a permanent fix rather than being re-investigated on every occurrence.
prevention_strategies: Right-size CI parallelism (-j flag) to the runner's physical memory for Windows Release/CC builds; add a monitoring check that fails fast with a clear infra-OOM message rather than cascading into tens of FAILED compilation units; consider dedicated higher-memory runners for Windows Conditional Compilation jobs given its history of recurrent OOM.
historical_context: Identical signature recorded 14 times previously between 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-19 (runs including 44603426744, 44599895950, 44588231549, 44581373590, 44292102363, 44238082087, 44082333313, 43907658756, 43398622571, 43369333911). No permanent fix has yet landed; this remains an open, unresolved recurring infrastructure problem.
